Hi Rachel,

Thanks for sending the invite. We tried to accept it this morning but ran into two problems: the link opens, we enter the OTP, and then the page immediately redirects back to the login with an error that says "session rejected: device fingerprint mismatch". We tested on Chrome on Windows and Safari on an iPhone — same outcome.

I've attached a screenshot of the error and a tiny export of the console logs from the browser. Can you check if there's a setting on your side that would block our requests? We are behind a corporate proxy but can try from a home network if helpful.

Hi Kristin — sorry you're hitting that. Appreciate the screenshots; that "device fingerprint mismatch" wording is coming from an anti-fraud check in the portal when the browser or proxy modifies identifying headers. A few quick asks/steps while we investigate: 

- Can you try accepting the invite in an incognito/private window and from a different network (personal hotspot or home network)?
- If that fails, please paste the full error string exactly as shown (screenshots are great, but the raw text helps).
- We're going to issue a one-time alternate invite URL that bypasses the device-fingerprint check and sends a direct magic-link to the account email — please expect that in ~15 mins.

Sean / Priyom — looping you in because this looks like the anti-fraud rule firing for Acme's tenant. If we can temporarily relax the fingerprint requirement for ACME-2027-0012 or whitelist their IP range for the invite flow that should fix it. Priyom, can you check the invite middleware logs and see which rule ID fired?

Kristin, I realize the PO timeline is tight; we'll prioritize.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Rachel / Sean — I pulled the invite middleware trace for ACME-2027-0012 (logs attached). The rule that triggered is 'FP_MATCH_STRICT_V2' — it flags mismatches between the original invite fingerprint and the final session headers when proxies rewrite UA or when the mobile webview strips certain headers. The server debug shows header delta: user-agent and x-forwarded-for changed between steps.

Short-term options (pick one):
1) Issue a one-time bypass invite URL (no device-fingerprint check) — low-risk for a single-use link that expires in 6 hours.
2) Send an SSO/Workday-style external link that routes to our IDP with SAML request (they would need an IdP partner) — heavier and slower.
3) Request Acme to accept via a desktop browser on an unmanaged network (not ideal for them).

I'll generate the one-time bypass link now and paste it into this thread; Rachel, please confirm before I send. Also including server-debug-log.txt with the precise trace for your security team if needed.

— Priyom
Engineering (Onboarding Tools) | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: server-debug-log.txt)
